action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.status: OK; Setup step; model not called.

info.agentSelfReportedStatus: OK; Setup step; model not called.

1.  **Board Analysis**:
    *   Player x pieces: (5,3), (5,4)
    *   Player o piece: (4,3)
    *   The columns are 0-indexed, so columns 3 and 4 are the most central.

2.  **Evaluating o's Options**:
    *   **Column 4**: Playing here will place o's piece at (4,4) because (5,4) is already occupied by x. This move creates a horizontal pair for o (4,3 and 4,4) in the center of the board. It also blocks x's vertical potential in column 4 and places o in a strong position to control the center.
    *   **Column 3**: Playing here would place o at (3,3), creating a vertical pair (4,3 and 3,3). While strong, it doesn't block x's potential vertical development in column 4.
    *   **Column 2**: Playing here would place o at (5,2), blocking one side of x's potential horizontal row (5,2-5,5). However, this is on the bottom row and is less central than (4,4).

3.  **Strategy**:
    *   Controlling the center (columns 2, 3, and 4) is the most effective opening strategy in Connect Four.
    *   Column 4 is a highly proactive move. It balances the board by mirroring x's horizontal presence but at a more advantageous height (Row 4). By occupying (4,4), o blocks x from developing vertically in that column and sets up multiple diagonal and horizontal opportunities for themselves.

4.  **Conclusion**:
    Column 4 is the most balanced and strategically sound move for player o at this stage, focusing on center control, blocking the opponent, and building future connections.

The current position has x pieces at bottom of columns 3 and 4, with o pieces directly on top of them in row 4. This is x's third move. No player can win immediately on this turn (x will have only 3 pieces afterward).

Dropping in column 2 places an x at (5,2), creating three consecutive x's along the bottom row in columns 2-4. Both ends of this line are completely open at the bottom (columns 1 and 5). This creates an immediate forced win: o can block at most one end on the next turn, after which x extends the other end (e.g., if o blocks column 1 then x plays column 5, or vice versa) to complete four consecutive x's along the bottom and win on the following turn. o cannot create any winning threat of their own on this turn (o will have only 3 pieces and cannot reach an unblocked 4-in-a-row in one move, especially since extending o's row-4 line requires bottoms to be pre-filled in adjacent columns).

The same forced win exists by playing column 5 instead (creating bottom x's in columns 3-5, with open ends at columns 2 and 6). Both are optimal winning moves; column 2 is selected here as it creates the more centrally controlled winning lines.
